description: About Us Higharc is a VC-backed startup that is changing how new homes are designed and built. Join a founding team who’ve shipped products for Autodesk, Electronic Arts, Nike, and Apple. We have raised over $175M with support from top-notch venture capital firms and more than 18 strategic investors: industry leaders in construction, building products manufacturing, and distribution. Higharc is seeking an accomplished UX Designer to join our growing Product org. In this role, you'll define and craft end-to-end experiences that simplify the complex—and make home design and construction more accessible, efficient, and human. What You'll Do You’ll work alongside a multidisciplinary team of engineers, architects, and 3D visualization experts to design tools that serve builders, buyers, and everyone involved in bringing homes to life. Your work will have a lasting, real-world impact and play a critical role in shaping the future of the homebuilding industry. Expect to: Design End-to-End Experiences: Lead the UX and UI design of web-based tools across Higharc ’s platform. Simplify the Complex: Translate detailed workflows into clear, human-centered experiences. Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Work closely with product managers and engineers to ensure cohesive product thinking. Partner closely with homebuilders, suppliers, contractors, and buyers to understand their needs and pain points. Own Design Process: Develop user flows, journey maps, wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity visuals to articulate design intent. Influence Product Strategy: Bring a strong, user-focused design perspective to product decisions. Validate with Data: Leverage both qualitative and quantitative user insights to inform and iterate on designs. Champion Design Systems: Contribute to and evolve our design system to ensure consistency and scalability. About You You’re a product-minded designer who thrives on solving complex problems and crafting user-centered solutions. You’re passionate about improving how people design and live in their homes—and energized by the opportunity to make a meaningful dent in an outdated industry. You have: 7+ years of experience designing web-based software A track record of shipping high-quality, thoughtful product experiences in complex domains A strong portfolio that showcases your process, thinking, and ability to simplify complexity Deep user empathy and a clear, confident communication style—especially when working with cross-functional teams A systems-thinking mindset with the ability to balance detail with big-picture product vision Experience in defining and delivering net-new experiences, not just iterating on existing patterns Comfort articulating trade-offs, managing ambiguity, and driving toward clarity in fast-moving environments A major plus if you also bring: A background or passion in architecture, construction tech, or home design Familiarity with 3D tools or environments (e.g., Revit, Rhino, SketchUp, Unity, Three.js) Experience contributing to or evolving a design system Working at Higharc Remote work and travel: Our company is entirely remote, and has been since we were founded in 2018. Remote work means more time with family, less time commuting, and the flexibility to blend work and life. We value in-person collaboration and asynchronous deep-work time, which is why we schedule regular team meet-ups in our hubs across the US and, depending on the role, prioritize hiring in those hubs. If your role requires frequent travel beyond pre-scheduled team meet ups, we will represent that to the best of our ability as early as possible in the interview process. Compensation and benefits: Higharc offers competitive salaries with significant equity, in a fast-growing, well-funded company. We provide comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with flexible PTO, and meaningful maternity/paternity leave to all U.S based employees that are full-time. You'll also have access to other big-company benefits such like short and long-term disability plans and a 401K. We also provide a stipend to create the ideal home office and support ongoing L&D. Please note: we are seeing an uptick of fraudulent recruiting activity claiming to be associated with Higharc . All communication and outreach from our in-house team will come from an @higharc.com email address. Originally posted on Himalayas

Binance is a leading global blockchain ecosystem behind the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume and registered users. About the Role: Binance Risk Operation team is seeking an experienced Risk Operations Specialist to implement effective risk control for the Binance platform and its users. You will be responsible for reviewing a range of predetermined alerts, as well as service requests, to determine whether recent account activity may be fraudulent in nature. You will carry out investigations using multiple resources, including customer contact, reviewing account activity, assessing phone number matching, IP searches, and various online tools. Risk Operations Specialists are customer-focused and aim to enhance customers’ understanding of our account processes. At the same time, you will educate customers on maintaining account security and work to prevent losses for both the company and its users. You will be responsible for reviewing documentation, analysing data, and making timely decisions on whether to verify the authenticity of transactions and/or activities. Throughout this process, you may need to communicate with customers to request additional information or to notify them of outcomes. A Risk Operations Specialist is organised, efficient, and motivated, demonstrates strong analytical skills, adapts well to change, and thrives in a collaborative team environment. This position will operate in alignment with US time zone and requires shift-based operation, including potential weekends and public holidays. What You’ll Do: Review and investigate risk-related cases, including KYC verification, account takeover concerns, two-factor authentication resets, withdrawal reviews, and abnormal trading activities (60%). Monitor account activity to detect unusual or suspicious behaviour and take appropriate action to prevent fraudulent or unauthorized transactions (15%). Contact account holders to verify account activity, investigate concerns, and mitigate potential losses (10%). Assess suspicious activities, identify potential risk indicators, and make timely, well-reasoned decisions in accordance with established procedures (10%). Maintain accurate and comprehensive case documentation to support auditability and quality assurance (5%) What We’re Looking For: Minimum of 3–5 years of proven experience in high-risk, rule-based, or process-driven environments, preferably within financial services, fraud prevention, risk management, or compliance. Work independently with minimal supervision, taking full ownership of assigned cases and responsibility Flexible and willing to support weekend coverage as part of a team operating on a 7-day schedule. Hands-on experience conducting KYC (Know Your Customer), KYB (Know Your Business), account take over and transaction-related investigations. Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to identify patterns, anomalies, and potential risks within transaction data. Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to produce clear, concise, and well-supported case documentation and recommendations. Proven ability to make sound judgment calls and risk-based decisions in ambiguous situations while working with minimal supervision. Demonstrated ability to maintain a high level of accuracy, consistency, and attention to detail while performing effectively under pressure and managing competing priorities. This is a remote position open to candidates residing in Mexico. You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. job_title: Staff Tech Enablement Engineer, B2B Operations
description: About CookUnity : Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul. Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world. If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting. About the Team: As part of our B2B Operations, the Tech Enablement team serves as a central tech hub connecting Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, CX, and Operations. We focus on building internal tools and automations that streamline workflows and reduce manual work across teams. By unifying systems and data and leveraging a mix of low-code platforms and custom development, Tech Enablement drives efficiency and scalable growth for CookUnity’s B2B business. This small, cross-functional team wears many hats – from creating process automations and integrations, to building and maintaining smart hardware solutions – all in the service of empowering our Ops team and other departments to work smarter and faster. The role: We are looking for a Staff Tech Enablement Engineer to lead the technology that supports CookUnity's B2B operations and Smart Fridges program. You will manage and develop a Tech Enablement Engineer, work hands-on with the engineer covering Smart Fridges hardware and OS, and collaborate with Product, Engineering, Operations, Healthcare, Sales, Marketing, and CX leaders. You will own the direction and reliability of our internal tools, automations, and integrations while leading the hardware and operating-system work needed to deploy and support hundreds of Smart Fridges. This is a hands-on leadership role. You will set priorities and technical standards, review architecture and code, investigate difficult software and device issues, and make sure each solution has a clear owner and support model. You will help the team move quickly without creating fragile workflows, undocumented devices, or systems that cannot be operated safely at scale. Responsibilities: Team Leadership & Prioritization: Manage, coach, and develop the Tech Enablement Engineer. Own intake, capacity, roadmap, delivery commitments, and communication with B2B and Product & Engineering leaders. Make tradeoffs visible and focus the team on measurable business impact. Build & Optimize Automations: Lead the design, delivery, and operation of workflows that remove manual work across B2B. Use low-code tools such as n8n and custom software where each is appropriate. Ensure critical jobs have monitoring, failure handling, recovery paths, and clear ownership. Full-Stack Internal Tools: Guide the development of internal web and mobile tools, dashboards, and services for Operations, Healthcare, CX, Sales, and Smart Fridges. Contribute directly to complex work, establish sound engineering practices, and decide when a prototype needs to become a supported product. Hardware (IoT) & Smart Fridge OS: Own the technical direction for Smart Fridges hardware and embedded Linux software alongside the hardware engineer. Work across compute devices, locks, sensors, cameras, connectivity, and on-device computer vision. Partner with manufacturers and field teams on component choices, build quality, installation, device debugging, and failure analysis. Fleet Scale & Reliability: Turn one-device-at-a-time setup and updates into repeatable imaging, enrollment, remote deployment, staged releases, rollback, and central fleet-health monitoring. Define release gates, security controls, and operational measures so hundreds of fridges can be deployed, updated, and supported without proportional growth in manual work or site visits. Third-Party Integrations: Lead reliable data flows between CookUnity systems and platforms such as Salesforce, support tools, logistics services, and healthcare partners. Work with system owners on API and webhook contracts, data quality, credentials, and incident response. Security & Operational Readiness: Partner with Security, Legal, Infrastructure, and Engineering on access, secrets, auditability, and reviews for customer and healthcare data. Build runbooks, alerting, and recovery procedures for business-critical workflows and field devices. Documentation & Handover: Keep source-of-truth links, architecture decisions, device build and release procedures, deployment steps, and operational playbooks current. Decide with Product and Engineering which services Tech Enablement will maintain, which prototypes should be productized, and which should be retired. AI Tools & Agents: Identify practical opportunities to use AI in B2B operations and engineering workflows. Evaluate prototypes for measurable value, reliability, data protection, and a sustainable owner before scaling them. Minimum requirements : Experience managing engineers, including coaching, feedback, prioritization, and accountability for delivery. Strong hands-on software engineering experience across backend services, integrations, and internal applications, with proficiency in JavaScript/TypeScript or Python and working knowledge of SQL. Hands-on experience building and operating physical devices with embedded Linux or comparable IoT software in the field. You can diagnose problems across device hardware, sensors, connectivity, operating-system services, and cloud systems. Demonstrated experience scaling a device fleet beyond hand-configured deployments, including reproducible provisioning, remote software updates, staged releases and rollback, telemetry, security, and field support. Experience designing reliable production workflows using APIs, webhooks, scheduled jobs, and third-party systems, including retries, idempotency, monitoring, and data reconciliation. Experience with cloud deployment, CI/CD, access management, and incident response for systems that business teams depend on. Sound judgment about security and privacy, including when to involve specialist reviewers for sensitive customer or healthcare data. Ability to turn ambiguous operational needs into priorities, technical plans, and clear decisions with technical and non-technical stakeholders. Helping to have higher levels of uptime & supporting the on-call rotation that will help the business run 24/7 Fluent English communication skills , written and spoken, for collaboration across teams and regions. Preferred requirements: Experience with Raspberry Pi or similar edge devices, and with AWS IoT Greengrass, SSM, MQTT, or comparable fleet-management tools. Experience with camera pipelines, computer vision at the edge, hardware manufacturing, or device quality assurance. Experience with n8n or similar automation platforms and with Salesforce or other CRM integrations. Experience building internal applications with React/Next.js and Node.js or Python, and deploying them on cloud platforms. Familiarity with healthcare operations or workflows involving PHI-sensitive data. Experience with customer support, marketing, or logistics tools and their APIs. Experience applying AI tools to operational workflows while checking output quality, privacy, and business impact. Comfort leading a small team across software, hardware, vendors, and business stakeholders in a fast-moving environment. Benefits: 💸 Get paid in USD. 🗺 Work remotely: design the life that you want. ⛱ Enjoy 15 business days of vacation each year from the start date. 🎄16 fully paid Argentinean holidays. 🩺 Healthcare Benefit: Monthly stipend to use in your preferred healthcare provider. 🗓️ 5-year Sabbatical: After 5 years with CookUnity, you get a 4-week paid sabbatical. 🐣 Paid family leave. 🕯 Compassionate Leave: 3-5 days each time the need arises. 🧘🏽‍♀️ Customize the benefits that suit your needs! Access a range of perks tailored to you, including learning opportunities, wellness memberships, delivery apps, and more through our comprehensive benefit platform. 🧑‍🏫 Personalized English coach. #LI-Hybrid If you’re interested in this role, please submit your application, and if we think you might be a fit, we'll get in touch with you. Thank you for your time! CookUnity is an Equal Opportunity Employer . We are dedicated to creating a community of inclusion and an environment free from discrimination or harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or physical or mental disability. A quick note for all candidates We’ve recently seen an increase in recruitment scams across the industry, and we want to make sure you (and your data) stay safe while applying to CookUnity. We also want you to know that we take this seriously — sometimes, as part of our process, we may ask for a brief “proof of humanity” to confirm that we’re connecting with a real person, not an impersonator. Here are a few tips to help you protect yourself and know what to expect from us: Apply only through our official channels. All open roles are listed on our official careers page: careers.cookunity.com Our recruiters are real people — and easy to verify. You can always find them on LinkedIn with verified profiles. If you’re unsure, feel free to reach out to us on our official LinkedIn Company Page . We only communicate through official CookUnity channels. That means emails ending in @cookunity.com and interviews held through official company platforms (Google Meet or Zoom) — never WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS. We’ll never ask for payment or personal financial details. If anyone does, please don’t share any information and let us know right away. If something ever feels off or you’re unsure about a message, we’d much rather you double-check with us. You can always contact us directly through any of our social media channels. We appreciate your interest in joining CookUnity — and we care about keeping your experience (and safety) as genuine as possible.

About 3Y Health 3Y Health is building the operating system for healthcare practices, an AI-native platform that helps clinicians start, run and grow their practice. We work as a managed services organization (MSO): along with the software, our operations team runs the back office for the clinics we partner with, including billing, insurance and compliance. We currently serve applied behavior analysis (ABA) therapy practices and are expanding into speech, occupational and physical therapy, and psychiatry. About the role Members of Technical Staff own features end to end. You'll work with the clinicians and operators who use what we build, scope the problem, design and build the solution across the stack, deploy it and follow how it performs in production. Our engineering team is flat, with no sub-teams, so you'll work across the whole platform. We build with AI coding agents every day and expect you to do the same. What you'll do Design and build AI agents and automated workflows for clinic operations, such as insurance benefits verification, prior authorizations, patient intake, claims and clinical documentation Build features for clinicians, patients and families, and our internal operations team, on web and mobile Take ambiguous problems from 0 to 1, working with operators and clinicians to define the problem, write the spec and ship a first version Design the services, data models and APIs behind your features and manage the infrastructure as code Own your services in production: deployments, monitoring and incident response Write evals for model-facing features and track the metrics of the workflows you ship Work with protected health information (PHI) safely, with least-privilege access, no PHI in logs and auditable changes Build and maintain the skills, plugins, MCP integrations and review bots our engineers use with Claude Code and Codex Our stack Backend: Python (our primary language for new services), Kotlin with Hasura (GraphQL) on our established platform, plus TypeScript (NestJS) and some Go Frontend and mobile: React, Next.js, React Native Data: PostgreSQL (including pgvector), Snowflake Workflows and contracts: Temporal, gRPC/Protobuf Infrastructure: AWS (ECS Fargate, RDS), Terraform, GitHub Actions, Datadog, LaunchDarkly AI: Claude and OpenAI models, Claude Code and Codex, with our own skills, plugins, MCP integrations and an AI code-review bot Must-haves 5+ years of experience building and shipping production software Recent, hands-on experience using or building AI harnesses: the layer around a model or coding agent (project instructions, tools and MCP servers, skills, hooks, subagents, evals), not only calls to a model API. You can show what you set up or built. At least one personal project you built and published on the web, live and usable by anyone, ideally a SaaS with payments working (e.g. Stripe). Share the link when you apply. What we're looking for A track record of owning products or features end to end, from an unclear problem to a system people depend on Strong full-stack skills in Python and TypeScript, with experience across frontend, backend, databases and cloud infrastructure Comfort working in a large, established codebase Hands-on experience building with LLMs, including tool use, agent orchestration, structured outputs, retrieval and evals (LangGraph, an agents SDK or similar) Daily use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. You know how to set them up for a codebase (project instructions, skills, MCP servers, hooks, subagents), run several tasks in parallel and review their output carefully. If you haven't heard of Claude Code, this role is likely not a fit. Good product sense and the ability to make solid UI decisions without a dedicated designer, using our component library High agency: you unblock yourself, look for context and ask questions when you need to Clear written communication. The team is distributed across time zones and most decisions happen in specs, PRs and tickets. Nice to have Experience in healthcare or another regulated industry (HIPAA, payer and claims workflows, EHR integrations, HL7/FHIR) Temporal or another durable workflow engine React Native Running LLM evaluations or safety checks on model output in production Having built your own agent harness, MCP server or plugin for a coding agent Open-source work or internal tools that other people use If you meet all the must-haves and most of the rest, we'd like to hear from you, even if you don't check every other box.

Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. This is a remote position and we're considering candidates in the UK, Spain or Ireland. The Opportunity About our platform Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. We aim to grow this to hundreds of millions per second, and it's critical that as we grow, we improve our performance, increase our reliability, and do it efficiently and securely. The Foundations department owns the Internal Engineering Platform (IEP): the Kubernetes clusters, cloud service provider resources (CSP), hardware, identity, delivery, and observability systems that Grafana Labs's application engineers use to build, deploy, and run their workloads. About the Infrastructure group We're hiring an engineering manager for the Foundations Infrastructure group, which owns the cloud infrastructure Grafana Cloud runs on. The group provisions and operates Kubernetes clusters and CSP resources across GCP, AWS, and Azure; enforces identity, access, and security controls across those environments; and runs the observability and cost-visibility systems that keep the infrastructure measurable and accountable. You'll lead one of the squads of platform engineers that comprise the group. We're platform engineers, and our application teams are our users. Our job is to give them leverage: self-service building blocks that take care of the hard parts of infrastructure, so they can focus on what they're building. We treat the platform as a product and value the experience of the people who use it. When a change is well communicated and understood, teams welcome it, and it lands as an improvement that makes the right way the easy way. You'll lead a squad that makes that happen. How we work Foundations is a global team that works asynchronously. The people who own a component or problem make the decisions about it, once stakeholders have had a chance to weigh in. Application teams build and run their own services; we give them a self-service platform to do it on. Every engineer is on-call for the components their squad provides. We plan on-call, tactical work, and time off into every quarter, so roadmap work is roughly half of an engineer's time rather than all of it. What You'll Be Doing Hire, manage, and develop a squad of platform engineers, with regular feedback and career conversations that support each person's growth. Own your squad's roadmap and quarterly objectives: help decide what the squad works on, what it defers, and why, across a broad remit where demand always exceeds capacity. Take platform changes from design to fleet-wide adoption: staged rollouts, migration paths, and clear communication, so changes land well for the teams who depend on them. Partner with the other Infrastructure squads on work that spans them, and with the teams across Foundations and the rest of Engineering whose work depends on yours. Help shape how the group works as a whole, including planning, on-call, and the ownership model between squads. Own the squad's intake. Requests, reviews, and support from application teams arrive continuously; keep them triaged and visible so that planned work still moves. Keep on-call healthy: ensure a sustainable load and support incident response. Work across team boundaries, contributing beyond your squad's scope where Foundations needs it. We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction. We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups, always paired with strong code review and quality standards. What Makes You a Great Fit Experience managing engineers, ideally a team that builds and operates production CSP infrastructure, security, networking and/or storage Hands-on depth in at least one area of platform engineering, such as cloud infrastructure and Kubernetes, infrastructure security and access, or observability. You can challenge a design in your area on its merits, and the engineers on your team will expect you to. Fluency with infrastructure as code and with running Kubernetes in production. A track record of landing internal engineering/developer platform changes at scale. You've driven a migration or a rollout across many teams or many clusters, and you know what makes one stall. The ability to explain platform engineering to very different audiences (platform engineers, application teams, product management and business leadership) and to make the case for what the squad should and shouldn't take on. Be comfortable collaborating across time zones and cultures in a fully remote environment, using clear, written communication to build trust and psychological safety. You're a motivated self-starter with a strong bias toward action and ownership, able to navigate ambiguity in a complex problem space. Comfort with AI-assisted tooling. We embrace AI and agentic development, so we expect you to be curious and comfortable using AI-powered tools, and ideally to have practical experience folding them into a team's workflow. Bonus Points For Experience across more than one of the group's areas: cloud infrastructure, infrastructure security, and observability Hands-on depth in cloud infrastructure security: cloud IAM, Kubernetes security, secrets, and workload identity on at least one major cloud provider. You can challenge a threat model or an access design on its merits, and the engineers on your team will expect you to. Building self-service infrastructure for application teams Running observability for a production platform at scale Operating across more than one of GCP, AWS, and Azure You've worked in or on open source, or other community-based projects. At Grafana Labs, "OSS is in our DNA" In Ireland, the base compensation range for this role is €121,128 - €145,354. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. #LI-Remote *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment. Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates. The agency and no-nonsense approach of a seed startup: you write product specs, make product and design decisions, and build in an almost-no-meeting culture. We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. We’ll share more details once we meet. You’ll join our Security team, a single team with multiple specializations overseeing security across the business. I report to Abhik, our Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re bubbling with ideas for how to support Talent Acquisition with software, and we recently launched Talent Management products to expand our total addressable market and become a company worth $60B+. We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner). Role Overview An employee’s access is increasingly also the access they can delegate to an AI tool. That makes identity and permissions an engineering problem with a practical question behind it: can we understand what someone or their agent can reach, and reconstruct what happened when something goes wrong? We’re looking for someone who can build the systems that answer that question. You’ll automate access management, connect the evidence needed for investigations, and improve the security workflows our team uses every day. You’ll care about how those controls feel to the people using them as well as the risks they address. About the Role and How We Work Your mission is to automate and scale internal security access management while giving us the visibility and response capability to investigate incidents. You’ll own security integrations, identity workflows, operational telemetry, and automation across the internal environment, and incident management for the Security team. You’ll work closely with IT on access management and logging, with Engineering on service and agent identities, with Infrastructure on cloud signals, and with GRC on control requirements and AI governance evidence. GRC will run routine vendor diligence; you’ll provide deeper technical review when data sensitivity, privileged access, integration scope, or service criticality warrants it. You’ll own the security logic and automation connecting these systems and be the Security team’s sole owner for incident management. You’ll lead intake, triage, coordination, escalation, and follow-through. Application Security will own product authorization and AI-feature threat modeling and contribute specialist analysis during incidents. Together, you’ll make internal access decisions and investigations coherent across human, service, and agent activity. In practice, you’ll: Automate identity lifecycle and access changes, including joiner, mover, and leaver workflows, access reviews, expiring grants, and integrations with internal systems. Help define prohibited combinations of role, system, action, and data, then implement access controls and monitoring proportionate to the risk. Evaluate and extend contextual access controls that assess each request using current identity, device posture, and relevant behavioral signals. Compare how Okta and Cloudflare can support those decisions across internal systems. Centralize useful telemetry from identity, SaaS, infrastructure, repositories, and data systems. Define and maintain detections and escalation rules with our outsourced SOC, improving them through incident learnings. Evaluate SIEM options through a practical proof of concept, including Datadog Cloud SIEM, Microsoft Sentinel, and Splunk, then recommend an approach based on coverage, investigation quality, effort, and cost. Build agent attribution: connect the initiating human, acting agent, credentials and permissions, trigger, and resulting actions so activity can be reconstructed. Deliver useful alerts and permitted response actions through Slack, with access checks, confirmation where needed, and an audit trail. Use AI to help with enrichment and triage while retaining accountability for consequential decisions. Own incident management from preparation and intake through severity assessment, containment and recovery coordination, stakeholder updates, post-incident review, and tracking follow-up actions to closure. Build the evidence capture, playbooks, and automation that make investigations faster and more reliable. To ground it with examples, you could: Build an access workflow that grants an appropriate capability for a limited period and automatically removes it, with the reason and owner attached. Follow an agent’s repository or infrastructure action back to the human who initiated it and show the permissions it used. Connect identity and SaaS events to an alert that gives an investigator enough context to act, then test whether the detection works without flooding the team with routine activity. Why You Should and Shouldn’t Apply You should apply if: You’ve built integrations, internal tools, or automation for identity, security operations, or enterprise systems, and you can write maintainable code. You understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, and how access and delegation work across cloud and SaaS systems. You’ve worked with logs, detections, and incident investigations, coordinated a security incident through resolution, and know what evidence a responder needs to reconstruct an event. You care about the experience of employees using security controls, and you can use data to stage changes and find workflows that need a better path. You’ve applied AI or workflow automation to operational work and can explain the limits, permissions, and review points of what you built. You collaborate well with IT, Infrastructure, engineers, and nontechnical teams, and can own a problem across those boundaries. You might not enjoy the role if: You want to spend most of your time administering consoles. We want you to build integrations and automate recurring work. You believe access should always be blocked or always be monitored. You’ll need to make the tradeoff explicit and implement the appropriate treatment. You want to collect every log before deciding what to detect. We’ll start with risks and the evidence needed to investigate them. You want AI agents to make consequential access or response decisions without traceability. Delegation has to preserve accountability. You only want project work. Incident management, investigations, response, tuning, and maintenance are part of the job. Level and Experience This posting is aimed at Senior engineers, and we’re also open to Staff-level candidates. We care about the systems you’ve built, the judgment you bring, and your ability to own a problem through implementation and operation. At Senior level, we expect you to independently deliver substantial security work and help other engineers use what you build. At Staff level, we expect experience setting technical direction across teams, finding recurring problems, and building approaches that others can extend. Your First Three Months at Ashby Your early changes will give you a tour of our codebase, infrastructure, and best practices, increasing in scope and ambiguity as you learn how we work. Early on, you could: Map key access paths, service and agent identities, and missing investigation evidence with IT and Engineering. Propose the initial prohibited access combinations and assess Okta and Cloudflare against contextual-access requirements. Run a SIEM proof of concept using representative identity, SaaS, cloud, and repository signals, comparing coverage and operational cost. Establish incident intake, severity and escalation criteria, response playbooks, and follow-up ownership; test an initial Slack investigation workflow and agent-attribution path, and define when vendor diligence needs a technical security review. Role-Specific Technology and Tools For this role, identity protocols, APIs, event data, and production automation matter more than one vendor certification. Okta, Cloudflare, GitHub, Google Workspace, and cloud logs are relevant to the environment. We’ll evaluate SIEM choices as part of the work. You should be comfortable building integrations and security workflows in a language such as TypeScript, Python, or Go. Benefits Competitive salary and equity. 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby; do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it. A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. The actual number may increase to satisfy local requirements. Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive! $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval. $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets. If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us. Closing Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply. Mozilla Foundation is the place to build good technology alternatives. We believe the future of technology should remain open, so more people, in more places, can shape what gets built and who benefits. To bring that ambition to life, we are evolving our current incubator into the Mozilla Studio. As our inaugural Vice President of Studio , you will lead Mozilla Foundation’s entrepreneurial engine: executing in our thesis areas, backing unconventional technologies early, and helping them become thriving alternatives to the technologies that currently dominate our lives. We are looking for a proven operator with a global perspective. Today, too many consequential decisions about technology are made by too few. Promising ideas struggle to find support because they are too early for markets, too unconventional for venture capital, too technically ambitious for traditional philanthropy, or just too different for commercial incentives. This is especially true for builders in the global majority. We think philanthropy can play a different role: We can take early bets on technologies that expand collective human agency, strengthen the commons, and create promising alternatives to dominant financing, ownership, and technology models. We want to help founders strengthen their interventions, deepen their relationships with the communities they serve – what we call product-community fit – and cultivate the operating and financial models that allow their work to thrive. In an era of tumult, we believe that defiant optimism and humble experimentation will see us through and help make many possible futures become real. The Studio turns those beliefs into bets on alternative tech products and organizations. The opportunity We are seeking an exceptional Vice President of Studio to lead the entrepreneurial engine of Mozilla Foundation. This is a role for a seasoned operator: someone who has grown organizations, worked shoulder to shoulder with technical founders, and knows what it takes to turn an ambitious idea into a functioning, sustainable organization or product. Our Studio will be known for providing high-quality support that helps exceptional founders across the world overcome their most consequential barriers to success. You’ll inherit an active portfolio to manage in current thesis areas, including our Democracy x AI and soon-to-be-launched Human-Scale AI initiatives, while building the next stage of the Studio’s model. You’ll serve as a trusted strategic partner to founders, providing hands-on support for organizational design, deployment, and growth. You’ll connect founders with outstanding engineers, product leaders, designers, entrepreneurs, and other specialists, activating your existing networks and the broader Mozilla communities worldwide to do so. You’ll design a scalable combination of cohort-based learning and tailored support. You’ll bring in Entrepreneurs-in-Residence, technical advisors, and operating partners to solve specific challenges. You’ll help founders develop credible and creative paths to sustainability, whether through earned revenue, institutional adoption, public funding, philanthropic support, community stewardship, or other mission-aligned models. Over your first six to nine months, you’ll build a small team: a Growth and Sustainment Lead, administrative support, and a bench of part-time technical partners and Entrepreneurs in Residence. Experience in activating the open-source community will be key.
